survey.notes: Top section shows battery banks (GMDSS, Emergency, Gen Start, Aux Service) each with dual fuses, feeding chargers or inverter through a dotted-boundary Battery Isolator Panel containing rotary switches SW11-SW16 and breakers CB1/CB2 (50A), with diamond wire-gauge callouts (70) on conductors to Port/Stbd Generator ISG units. This portion is a power_one_line topology. Lower section (LVPDU) is a classic distribution_schedule: metering (CT5, CT6, shunts, ammeter/voltmeter) feeds three panel column groups (PORT, center, STBD) each listing CB-id/rating/load-name rows, repeated for main loads and again for 'System Cooling' loads. A few relay-like elements (Re.0, Re7) and CP switch/HVIL signal tap sit between center and STBD columns. Title block and abbreviation legend confirmed. Some small tag text near CBx rows (e.g. 'BEL CAN BUS ISOLATORS', 'BEL-SYNC') too small to fully verify at this resolution - flagged as possibly illegible/ambiguous. Overall sheet mixes both major layout patterns, hence classified mixed.

composition.serve_who: This sheet (GMMS 108'-110b, "AUX 24V START/ AUX LV SUPPLY") is a mixed power one-line + LVPDU distribution schedule. Top half shows the four 24V house battery banks (GMDSS, Emergency, Gen Start, Aux Service) with fuses/chargers/isolator switches feeding the Battery Isolator Panel and onward to CBI Control and the Port/Stbd 112kW generator ISG units feeding the MPCS. Middle band shows the 24V/230V MAPS-style AC/DC converter feeding an isolator (continued DWG 110a) and the SHUNT#1/CT6/SHUNT#5 metering into the LVPDU. Bottom half is the LVPDU itself: three column groups (PORT, center, STBD) of breakers feeding named BAE-system/propulsion/cooling loads, confirming and extending engineer red-pen breaker facts already on file (CB1-CB23, CBx1-CBx20). Each row names its own served equipment per the engineer's load-map; the panel/bus structure itself belongs to the LVPDU infrastructure (owned by 625-bae-system hub as the BAE LV control panel).

infrastructure.system_name: Negative Bus (24V house battery common return)
facts: Common negative bus bar tying together the (-) terminals of all four house battery banks (GMDSS, Emergency, Gen Start, Aux Service) via their respective shunts (#2, #3, #4) and a direct Aux Service tap.

No dedicated node for this specific bus; attached to DC distribution infrastructure per bus-ownership rule since it is shared house-battery infrastructure, not a titled standalone system on this sheet.
Dotted rectangular enclosure containing rotary switches SW11-SW16 and breakers CB1/CB2 (50A), selecting which battery/source feeds the generator starter B+ circuits and CBI Control taps.
Owned as BAE-adjacent generator-start switching infrastructure; not itself a named equipment — placed as infrastructure per rule 3.

infrastructure.system_name: LVPDU (Low Voltage Power Distribution Unit) bus structure
facts: LVPDU is the BAE system's LV control panel per established fact (628-scu3 control_wiring note); this sheet's PORT/center/STBD breaker columns and their supply buses (fed via SHUNT#1/F9/SW10/CT6/SHUNT#5 metering chain) are the panel infrastructure, not a distinct piece of equipment.
Metering chain: SHUNT#1 500A/50mV -> F9 125A -> SW10 -> CT6 -> SHUNT#5 -> PORT bus -> CB1-CB4; ammeter (A) and voltmeter (V) with F 2A fuse monitor the + bus.
STBD supply bus separately feeds CB5-CB8 and the Re.0/Re7 relay branches.
Distribution bus for CBx13-CBx20 group is a further internal junction within the LVPDU STBD auxiliary section.
